newsitem.title: USA: COOLER AIR STILL NO THREAT FOR BRAZIL COFFEE - WSC.
newsitem.headline: COOLER AIR STILL NO THREAT FOR BRAZIL COFFEE - WSC.

text.p: Cool, high pressure currently in Argentina will pass out to sea just south of Brazil's coffee belt in the next few days, Weather Services Corp said in an update on Friday.
The system does appear large enough to bring cool air into the region, although no damaging cold is expected.
"As the high moves off the coast it will gradually weaken. However, it will bring somewhat cooler than normal conditions into the coffee belt, " WSC said.
Fair to partly cloudy skies were reported in main growing areas of the belt this morning. Temperatures were in the middle 50's to low 60's F (middle teens C).

Partly to variably cloudy skies are expected for the next seven days. Temperatures will be turning cooler over the weekend with lows in the middle 40's to low 50's F (7-11 C). Cooler conditions are expected for higher elevations.
Temperatures may average near to below normal through next Thursday, although there is still no damaging cold weather expected, according to WSC.
